metadata.title: Claude, Matter Briefing.
metadata.subtitle: What a Skill Actually Is
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: has Claude been quietly tracking a legal matter over time when it runs the matter-briefing skill? Take the mechanism apart — a folder holding one SKILL.md, read top to bottom, run against whatever's currently on record — and judge the design trade-off: consistency of a five-part read (posture, changes, deadline, questions, risk) purchased at the cost of anything that wasn't already on the record.

beats.narration_text: Here's the natural read: Claude has been quietly tracking this legal matter as it develops. Wrong mechanism. It was handed a file on the matter, once, when you asked. Let's crack open that file.

beats.narration_text: Here's the language trap. Say Claude has a matter-briefing skill, and the word 'skill' makes it sound like something running in the background — keeping tabs on the case as it moves, building up a memory of it. That's the natural read. It's the wrong mechanism.

shot.new_visual_element: SOUNDS LIKE IT'S BEEN KEEPING TABS

production_viz.label: SOUNDS LIKE IT'S BEEN KEEPING TABS
production_viz.caption: that's the natural read

beats.narration_text: Here's the test that gives it away. Delete the skill's folder — Claude doesn't forget one update on the matter, because it was never storing any. All that vanishes is one routine. There is no memory in the skill to lose in the first place.

Here's what's actually inside. A skill is a folder holding one file — SKILL.md. Matter-briefing's file is a set of instructions for turning whatever's currently on the record into one structured read: posture, what's changed, next deadline, open questions, and a risk check. One file, the whole routine.

Here's how it runs. Claude reads that file top to bottom, works through each step in the order it's written, and doesn't branch unless the file itself tells it to. Boring, deterministic, on purpose — the same path every time is what makes the output the same shape every time.

So a skill is a specification, not an ongoing watch. What that optimizes for: consistency — the same five-part read every time, posture, changes, deadline, questions, risk. What it sacrifices: anything that wasn't already on the record when you asked. Nothing new gets discovered by the read; nothing new arrives while it's running.

production_viz.label: SPEC, NOT AN ONGOING WATCH
production_viz.caption: the same five parts, every time

beats.narration_text: Which is why matter-briefing never gave Claude a memory of the case's history. What it guarantees is smaller and more useful: every run, Claude reads the same file and produces the same five-part read. That's the whole trick — the consistency is the product.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — SAME FILE, EVERY RUN

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — SAME FILE, EVERY RUN
production_viz.caption: same file, same five parts, every run

beats.narration_text: Which flips the way you read the output, in both directions. A sharp, complete-looking briefing doesn't prove Claude caught every development — the skill only compiles what's on the record, so a gap in the record shows up as a gap in the briefing. And a briefing that misses something obvious doesn't prove the skill is broken — the record it was handed may never have had it. Neither read is proof of anything about Claude; both are readings of the record you gave it.
A skill isn't Claude's memory of the case — it's a file of steps run against whatever's on the record right now. Same file, same five parts, every time.

props.quote: A skill isn't Claude's memory of the case — it's a file of steps run against whatever's on the record right now. Same file, same five parts, every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: pick one thing you brief someone on regularly — a project, a matter, a case. Write me a SKILL.md for it with the same five parts: current status, what's changed since last read, next deadline, open questions, risk. Then walk me through exactly what you'll do, in the order you'll do it, before you do it. Go deeper: ask the same model what parts of your briefings quietly depend on judgment you never wrote down — the calls a fresh reader of your SKILL.md would silently get wrong.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to build a matter-briefing skill for myself — a single SKILL.md file that any capable AI reads top to bottom and executes against whatever's currently on the record, producing the same structured output every run. Pick one thing I brief someone on regularly — a project, a client matter, a case (ask me which). Write me a SKILL.md for it with five sections: current status, what's changed since the last read, next deadline, open questions, and a risk check. Then walk me through exactly what you'll do, in the order you'll do it, before you do it — no branching unless the file tells you to branch.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: ask the same model what parts of your briefings quietly depend on judgment you never wrote down — the calls a fresh reader of your SKILL.md would silently get wrong, and how the file would have to change to catch them.
